implementation_notes: The Scala standard library implements the pattern directly: the scaladoc states that the exported methods implement tail calls via trampolining, with methods either returning their result through done or handing over with tailcall, and result running the trampoline - its own example is the mutually recursive isEven/isOdd pair. Use it whenever mutual recursion must be stack-safe and no extra dependency is wanted. @tailrec is not an alternative: it only applies to self-recursive calls and refuses to compile when that is not the case, which is exactly the mutual-recursion situation.
pitfalls: Forgetting .result leaves a TailRec value that never runs; the trampoline only executes when the value is forced.
A direct call inside the body - instead of wrapping it in tailcall - silently uses the JVM stack again at that edge.
Returning TailRec[A] changes every signature in the group, so mixing trampolined and plain functions in one algorithm produces type churn; convert the whole group or none of it.

variants.name: cats.Eval with defer (pure-FP library)
variants.implementation_notes: cats Eval is the pure-FP realization: Eval.now, Eval.later and Eval.always build deferred computations, Eval.defer is the suspension point that makes the recursion stack-safe, and the type's documentation states that its implementation provides stack-safety using trampolining, with memoisation available on demand. Choose it when cats is already a dependency and the deferred computation is a composable value rather than only a control-transfer trick; the stdlib TailCalls form stays the dependency-free default.
pitfalls: Dropping Eval.defer builds the whole chain eagerly before it is forced: the trampoline never starts and the chain is constructed on the stack.
Choosing now/later/always decides memoisation, so laziness becomes a semantic choice rather than an implementation detail - memoised steps retain their results and the memory that comes with them.
Bridging Eval and TailRec in one codebase doubles the suspension vocabulary for the same algorithm.
